title: Trade and Cargo Academy
description: The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Charleston District (SAC) has a new requirement for construction of a Trade and Cargo Academy at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (FLETC). The requirement will include hazardous material abatement and selective demolition of the current vacant 30,000 SF, three-story building, while preserving the existing main lobby and ensuring uninterrupted utility service to the occupied east wing. In its place, a new 28,400 SF, two-story, flood-resilient facility will be constructed. Due to poor soil quality and its location within FEMA Zone AE, the TCA will use a deep precast concrete pile foundation with pile-supported slabs, a heavy-duty steel frame to withstand high wind/seismic demands, a modern rainscreen envelope, and fully integrated building systems (HVAC, LED lighting, and security infrastructure). The interior will have space for instructional use on the first floor (including classrooms, an auditorium, and production spaces) and administrative open offices on the second floor. FLETC also has a requirement for the construction of a new Cargo Security and Seized Property Training Facility (CSSPTF), a separate one-story 5,985 SF facility purpose-built to support U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) training. Specifically designed for hands-on vehicle/cargo inspection, evidence processing, and simulated seized property storage, this site-adapted facility will also be elevated on a deep pile foundation to comply with stringent floodplain requirements. A key engineering focus for this site is the implementation of pile-supported stormwater piping under paved areas to mitigate soil settlement risks. Both facilities are engineered for a minimum 40-year operational lifespan, integrating highly durable, low-maintenance coastal materials, and will comply fully with the latest federal energy conservation standards, DHS security criteria, and 2021 building codes. These facilities are essential for the increased student enrollment and additional courses offered supporting FLETC Charleston.

The manometry probe (or catheter) required to operate the HRM system is a thin, flexible tube equipped with sensors, inserted through the nose or mouth into the gastrointestinal tract to measure muscle pressure and coordination. This new request is for a one-time firm-fixed-price contract to procure replacement manometry probes compatible with the HRM system that are at end of lifecycle. The supplies/services needed are: Manoscan ESO Z CATH X1 � Mfr. Part #: 3890 � Quantity of 4 Each HRM Catheter Extended WARRANTY 1 YEAR � Mfr. Part #: 80372 � Quantity of 4 Each Shipping and Handling (Estimated) � Quantity of 1 Each Unique characteristics that limit availability to only one source, with the reason no other supplies or services can be used: The ManoView manometry system is a proprietary platform that requires OEM manufactured ManoScan catheters for operation. These catheters utilize proprietary connectors, hardware interfaces, and system recognition features that are unique to Medtronic equipment. The HRM system requires OEM-compatible manometry probes to avoid calibration drift, invalid pressure profiles, and adverse impact on clinical decisions. Probes from non?OEM sources are not validated with this system�s firmware and sterile pathway, creating risk to patient safety and data integrity. Medical device accessories must be assessed in context of the parent device; compatibility and risk controls apply. Description of market research conducted and results or statement why it was not conducted: The CVAMC SPS initiated market research in December 2025 to determine the facility�s needs and market availability. The LB OEM provided an informal quote and none of the items were found to be offered on FSS contract. Additional market queries were conducted by the Contracting Specialist using SBA SBS, SAM.gov, GSA Advantage, VA NAC, and ADDS UP databases. There were multiple entries found for various types of catheters offered by others in the industry. None of those items are compatible with the Government owned HRM equipment at the facility and capable of meeting this requirement. The product NAICS code was not found in the NMR class waiver database. Direct contact was made with the LB OEM. The OEM confirmed the country of orgin (COO) for the equipment is Vietnam and that pricing is open market. They also identified three (3) SBA SBS verified SDVOSB authorized distributors. Due to the NMR findings, an SDVOSB, VOSB set-aside is prohibited. The VA and Rule of Two cannot be met. The SBA Rule of Two is obtainable. INSTALLATION: Vendor will provide delivery and assembly/installation of the shielding systems in the Cardiac Catheterization Lab located within James A. Haley VA Hospital at 13000 Bruce B. Wszelkie inne roboty niezbędne dla zaprojektowania i zrealizowania inwestycji. Wartość szacunkowa zamówienia powyżej 20 000 000 EUR

Project square footage is estimated at 2,400 SF. Structural Framing & Enclosure: Utilizing cold-formed metal framing, insulated metal wall panels, and structural steel support systems. Roofing: Installation of high-performance standing seam metal roofing, complete with prefinished gutters, downspouts, and weather barrier wraps. Specialized Systems: Installation of mechanical HVAC systems (including specialized 20-ton air conditioning systems), interior plumbing, lightning/grounding protection, and communication infrastructure. Fire Protection: A complete fire alarm-mass notification system and wet-pipe sprinkler suppression system. In addition to the base work described above, the solicitation will include the following option line items: 1. MAC Pad - Construct 1,167 SY concrete pad for the Material Assembly Center (MAC), required for constructing munitions, along with new asphalt pavement for access and egress to the facility's maintenance bays. - KNMD209086 Conventional Munitions Cube Storage Addition - Construct an addition to the Munitions Cube Storage Facility (B3552) utilizing conventional design and construction methods to support the F-22 mission. This project has a statutory cost limitation $14M for Unspecified Minor Military Construction (UMMC) Project � Adjustment of Dollar Limitations for Location pursuant to 10 USC �2805. Project square footage is estimated at 1,320 SF. Work covered in this project includes but is not limited to: Substructure & Enclosure: Micro-pile foundations, concrete wall structures, cast-in-place concrete slabs, and 12" thick concrete walls designed for high-hazard storage specifications. Framing & Roofing: Structural steel framing, roof joists, and standing seam metal roofing matching existing facility standards. Exterior Elements: Erection of new asphalt pavement adjacent to the existing facility access to provide adequate logistics and material handling access around the new facility addition. Specialized Protection: Maintenance facility lightning and grounding protection systems, along with integrated fire detection and alarm reporting systems connected back to the base reporting system. Secured Zone Access: Once the temporary security fencing is approved and accepted by the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR), no escort shall be required within the active secured work zone during construction, allowing the contractor to work within the secured boundary unimpeded. KNMD209085 Munitions Maintenance and Inspection (M&I) Facility - Construct a new Munitions Maintenance & Inspections facility by utilizing conventional design and construction methods to accommodate the facility mission. This project has a statutory cost limitation $14M for Unspecified Minor Military Construction (UMMC) Project � Adjustment of Dollar Limitations for Location pursuant to 10 USC �2805. Project square footage is estimated at 2,400 SF. Work covered in this project includes but is not limited to: Micro-pile Foundations: Specialized foundation engineering featuring micro-piles to mitigate challenging soil conditions and ensure seismic structural integrity. Cast-in-Place Concrete: Constructing robust concrete slab-on-grade, concrete walls, capping beams, and associated structural masonry elements. Structural Framing & Enclosure: Utilizing cold-formed metal framing, insulated metal wall panels, and structural steel support systems. Roofing: Installation of high-performance standing seam metal roofing, complete with prefinished gutters, downspouts, and weather barrier wraps. Specialized Systems: Installation of mechanical HVAC systems (including specialized 20-ton air conditioning systems), interior plumbing, lightning/grounding protection, and communication infrastructure. Fire Protection: A complete fire alarm-mass notification system and wet-pipe sprinkler suppression system. In addition to the base work described above, the solicitation will include the following option line items: 1. MAC Pad - Construct 1,167 SY concrete pad for the Material Assembly Center (MAC), required for constructing munitions, along with new asphalt pavement for access and egress to the facility's maintenance bays. - KNMD209086 Conventional Munitions Cube Storage Addition - Construct an addition to the Munitions Cube Storage Facility (B3552) utilizing conventional design and construction methods to support the F-22 mission. This project has a statutory cost limitation $14M for Unspecified Minor Military Construction (UMMC) Project � Adjustment of Dollar Limitations for Location pursuant to 10 USC �2805. Project square footage is estimated at 1,320 SF. Work covered in this project includes but is not limited to: Substructure & Enclosure: Micro-pile foundations, concrete wall structures, cast-in-place concrete slabs, and 12" thick concrete walls designed for high-hazard storage specifications. Framing & Roofing: Structural steel framing, roof joists, and standing seam metal roofing matching existing facility standards. Exterior Elements: Erection of new asphalt pavement adjacent to the existing facility access to provide adequate logistics and material handling access around the new facility addition. Specialized Protection: Maintenance facility lightning and grounding protection systems, along with integrated fire detection and alarm reporting systems connected back to the base reporting system. Escort Requirements: Escort personnel shall be required when erecting the temporary security fence, performing work occurring outside the temporary security fence, and connecting utilities to the existing system. Secured Zone Access: Once the temporary security fencing is approved and accepted by the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR), no escort shall be required within the active secured work zone during construction, allowing the contractor to work within the secured boundary unimpeded.
